newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's United to buy control of Mesbla.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's United to buy control of Mesbla.

text.p: United Comercio e Industria holding company, owned by businessman Ricardo Mansur, will buy 53 percent of local ailing retailer Mesbla, said an executive at Banco Pactual which is managing the company.
"The holding of Ricardo Mansur has given a promise to buy 53 percent of Mesbla's capital," said Pactual's executive Jose Paulo Amaral.
Amaral said the 53 percent stake in Mesbla consists of shares converted from about 558 million reais debt, which had been owed to private banks, suppliers and debenture holders.
United will pay the creditors 100 million reais over 15 years in annual installments with a two percent interest, Amaral said.
He said United will only pay 100 million reais to the creditors because it will have to pay off 350 million reais in Mesbla's tax debts.
"It is paying much less for the shares because it is buying a company with fiscal debts," Amaral said.
The sale will take place in 150 days under two conditions -- Mesbla has to renegotiate its fiscal debt and lift its bankruptcy filing, he added.
Only if these two conditions are not fulfilled, the sale will not take place, he said.
"This promise of buying is irrevocable," he said.

Once a leading local retailer, Mesbla filed for debt relief under a section of the bankruptcy law equivalent to Chapter 11 in the United States in 1995. Since October last year Mesbla has been managed by Banco Pactual, which was hired by the firm's main creditors to restructure the company.
Since Pactual began to administer Mesbla and seek a solution for the company, the market had speculated about potential buyers for the retailer.
Mansur acquired control of Casa Anglo, the holding company for Mappin department store chain, in August 1996 and was seen as the most likely candidate to assume control of Mesbla.

Regarding Mesbla shops, Amaral said they would become Mappin stores in Sao Paulo state and south of Sao Paulo. In Rio de Janeiro state and all states north of Rio de Janeiro, the shops will remain named Mesbla.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
